articles.title: Implant size distribution and mid-term outcomes of transfibular total ankle arthroplasty in a Japanese cohort.
articles.authors: Yano K, Ikari K, Koseki T, Tominaga A, Okazaki K
articles.population: Japanese patients with end-stage ankle arthritis undergoing transfibular total ankle arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 50 patients (51 ankles)
articles.outcomes: Implant size distribution, clinical outcomes (Self-Administered Foot Evaluation Questionnaire and ankle range of motion), radiological alignment, complications, and implant survival rate
articles.take_home: Transfibular total ankle arthroplasty produced good results in Japanese patients with smaller ankle bones, with implant survival rates of 98% at three years and 95.5% at four years. Patients experienced significant improvements in pain, function and ankle movement, with most requiring smaller implant sizes than typically used in Western populations.

articles.title: Association of polyethylene type with revision and dislocation risk following primary total hip arthroplasty: a population-based cohort study from the Danish Hip Arthroplasty Register.
articles.authors: Chabaita M, Iljazi A, Sorensen MS, Eriksson F, Overgaard S, Petersen MM
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty for osteoarthritis
articles.sample_size: 48,618 patients from 2000 to 2016
articles.outcomes: All-cause revision, dislocation, and cause-specific revision (infection and aseptic loosening) according to polyethylene type and femoral head size
articles.take_home: Highly cross-linked polyethylene was associated with lower rates of dislocation and revision surgery compared to standard polyethylene, particularly for larger implant sizes (32 mm and 36 mm heads), but showed no benefit for smaller 28 mm heads. The study suggests potential advantages of highly cross-linked polyethylene, though the observational design means caution is needed in interpreting results.

articles.title: Assessment of a Novel Radiographic Index and Functional Outcomes After Secondary Patellar Resurfacing: A Matched Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Carlisi G, Familiari F, Gasparini G, Vescio A, Deckard ER, Meneghini RM, et al.
articles.population: Patients with anterior knee pain following primary total knee arthroplasty without patellar resurfacing, compared with matched controls who had primary total knee arthroplasty without patellar resurfacing and no postoperative pain
articles.sample_size: 246 patients (82 with secondary patellar resurfacing, 164 controls)
articles.outcomes: Visual Analog Scale, Knee Society Score, and Oxford Knee Score showed statistically significant improvement in the secondary patellar resurfacing group (P < 0.005). A novel radiographic index called the GC Index showed sensitivity of 82.93% and specificity of 85.37% for predicting postoperative anterior knee pain.
articles.take_home: Patients with persistent anterior knee pain after knee replacement who underwent secondary patellar resurfacing showed meaningful improvements in pain and function scores. A new radiographic measurement called the GC Index may help identify which patients would benefit from this procedure, but this requires further testing.

articles.title: Cost Consequences of Enabling Technologies in Primary Total Hip Arthroplasty: A Propensity Matched Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Williams JL, Gonzalez-Bravo AE, Moriarty JP, Borah B, Taunton MJ, Sierra RJ, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 513 technology-assisted procedures matched 1:1 to 513 manual procedures
articles.outcomes: Index hospitalisation cost, 90-day postoperative cost, total episode-of-care cost, and length of stay
articles.take_home: Technology-assisted hip replacement surgery cost more than manual surgery, with higher costs during both the initial procedure and in the 90 days after surgery. Hospital stays were slightly shorter with technology use, but this did not lead to lower overall costs.

articles.title: Preoperative Medial Proximal Tibial Angle of Less Than 84 degrees Does Not Compromise Two-Year Clinical Outcomes After Unrestricted Kinematic Alignment Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Propensity Score-Matched Study.
articles.authors: Ng Y, Lim WSR, Lam LZL, Escarda JL, Lee M, Yeo SJ
articles.population: Patients undergoing total knee replacement in a Southeast Asian population, stratified by severity of tibial varus deformity
articles.sample_size: 238 kinematic alignment and 476 mechanically aligned total knee replacements with minimum two-year follow-up
articles.outcomes: Patient-reported outcome measures including Oxford Knee Score and Knee Society scores, patient satisfaction, radiological parameters, and revision-free survival at two years
articles.take_home: Patients with severe tibial varus treated with unrestricted kinematic alignment knee replacement achieved similar satisfaction and clinical outcomes to those with less severe deformity, with excellent two-year survival rates. This suggests that severe tibial varus deformity does not compromise results with this newer alignment technique.

articles.title: Peri-Incisional Blisters after Total Knee Arthroplasty: Risk Factors and Clinical Implications.
articles.authors: Weinblatt AI, Do HT, Mujaj A, Goodman SM, Chalmers BP, Blevins JL, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing elective primary total knee replacement at a single high-volume centre
articles.sample_size: 23,405 knee replacements in 20,035 patients between March 2016 and May 2022
articles.outcomes: Incidence of peri-incisional blistering within 30 days of surgery; risk factors for blister formation; association with reoperation and infection
articles.take_home: Blisters around the surgical wound occurred in 3.1% of knee replacements and were strongly linked to needing further surgery and infection. Being on blood thinners or having a BMI of 40 or more increased blister risk, whilst advanced wound dressings reduced it.

articles.title: Impact of Gastrointestinal Bleeding History on Postoperative Outcomes in Total Hip and Knee Arthroplasty: A Retrospective Analysis.
articles.authors: Botolin P, Helbing J, Khanuja HS, Patel NK, Goldman AH
articles.population: Adults undergoing total hip or total knee replacement, with and without a history of gastrointestinal bleeding in the two years before surgery
articles.sample_size: THA: 12,840 patients (6,420 with GI bleed history, 6,420 controls); TKA: 19,376 patients (9,688 with GI bleed history, 9,688 controls)
articles.outcomes: Periprosthetic joint infection, mechanical loosening, revision surgery, and medical complications up to two years after surgery
articles.take_home: Patients with a recent history of gastrointestinal bleeding who have hip or knee replacement surgery have a higher risk of complications within two years, including infection risk after knee replacement and loosening risk after hip replacement. The overall complication rates remained low, but the findings suggest these patients may need closer monitoring after surgery.

articles.title: Coronal Spinal Imbalance Dictated Side Preference in Symmetrically Well-Aligned Bilateral Total Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Siripullop T, Ngarmukos S, Jaruthien N, Amarase C, Tanavalee C, Somrak P, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing bilateral total knee replacement with symmetrically well-aligned lower limbs
articles.sample_size: 122 patients at final follow-up (mean age 69 years, 81.3% women)
articles.outcomes: Knee Society Score, Forgotten Joint Score, side preference in relation to spinal alignment, clinical outcomes at mean 35 months follow-up
articles.take_home: Patients with spinal imbalance tended to prefer and put more weight through the knee on the side their spine was shifted towards, whilst both groups with balanced and imbalanced spines showed significant improvements in knee function and pain after surgery.

articles.title: Heterogeneity of Quadriceps Muscle Volume in Knee Osteoarthritis: A Latent Profile Analysis and Its Clinical Implications for Arthroplasty Outcomes.
articles.authors: Yang Y, Zang W, Zhou Y, Chen Y, Waterson B, Zhu J, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using latent profile analysis
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary robot-assisted total knee replacement for knee osteoarthritis
articles.sample_size: 191 patients (76.4% women, mean age 67 years)
articles.outcomes: Quadriceps muscle volume phenotypes at baseline; pain (WOMAC and VAS scores) and range of motion at six months post-surgery
articles.take_home: Three distinct muscle phenotypes were identified based on quadriceps size before knee replacement surgery. Patients with preserved muscle had the best overall outcomes, whilst those with severe muscle wasting showed greater relative improvement, suggesting personalised rehabilitation approaches based on muscle status could optimise recovery.

articles.title: Interlocking plate compared with conventional pin fixation for undisplaced femoral neck fractures: a randomized controlled trial with radiostereometric analysis.
articles.authors: Hogevold M, Hansen MM, Brattgjerd JE, Rohrl SM
articles.population: Patients with undisplaced femoral neck fractures
articles.sample_size: 25 patients randomised (12 pins, 13 plates); 17 completed 52-week follow-up
articles.outcomes: Fracture motion measured by radiostereometric analysis; Harris Hip Score; EQ-5D questionnaire; Timed Up and Go test; pain and satisfaction; reoperation rates; complications including avascular necrosis and sub-trochanteric fractures
articles.take_home: Interlocking plates reduced twisting motion at the fracture site compared with pins during the 52-week healing period, but this did not lead to differences in how well patients recovered or their pain levels. The clinical benefit of this extra stability remains unclear.

articles.title: Patients Requiring both Lumbar Spinal Fusion and Total Hip Arthroplasty Have Delayed Clinically Relevant Global Improvement Timelines. Findings from a Propensity Score-Matched Analysis of Time to MCID.
articles.authors: Sauder N, Williams DL, Singh R, Khalameyzer A, Rahman T, Melnic CM, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty, with and without lumbar spinal fusion
articles.sample_size: 183 patients with both procedures; 732 matched control patients without spinal fusion
articles.outcomes: Time to minimal clinically important difference in PROMIS Global Physical, PROMIS Physical Function Short Form-10a, and HOOS-PS scores
articles.take_home: Patients needing both hip replacement and spinal fusion surgery took longer to recover than those having hip replacement alone, with delays of about 1 month. Having spinal fusion before hip replacement resulted in similar recovery times to hip replacement alone, but having hip replacement first led to the longest delays in recovery.

articles.title: What is the association between insulin dependence and the incidence of postoperative complications, perioperative glucose control, and five-year reoperation rates after total joint replacement?
articles.authors: Wong J, Umelo J, Ramirez G, Myers TG, Ginnetti JG, Thirukumaran CP, et al.
articles.population: Patients with diabetes mellitus undergoing primary total hip or knee replacement
articles.sample_size: 830 patients (351 insulin-dependent, 479 insulin-independent)
articles.outcomes: 90-day postoperative complications, perioperative glucose control, and five-year reoperation rates
articles.take_home: Patients with diabetes who require insulin had nearly three times higher odds of complications within 90 days of hip or knee replacement and poorer blood sugar control around the time of surgery compared to those not requiring insulin, although reoperation rates were similar between groups.

articles.title: Association of treatment method with mortality and functional outcome in patients with displaced femoral neck fracture: a cohort study of 60-69-year-old patients from the Swedish Hip Fracture Register.
articles.authors: Campenfeldt P, Hedstrom M, Olofsson O, Modig K, Al-Ani A
articles.population: Patients aged 60-69 years with displaced femoral neck fracture
articles.sample_size: 3,325 patients
articles.outcomes: 1-year mortality, 4-month functional outcomes (independent living and outdoor walking ability)
articles.take_home: Total hip replacement was associated with lower death rates compared to other treatments, particularly in older or less healthy patients. Healthier patients who had total hip replacement were more likely to maintain independent living and walking ability compared to those having other treatments.

articles.title: Early revision rate in robotic-assisted versus conventional total knee arthroplasty: a prospective cohort study 2021-2023 from the Finnish Arthroplasty Register.
articles.authors: Alakyla KJ, Sylvestersson E, Venalainen MS, Eskelinen AP, Jaroma A, Vayrynen O, et al.
articles.study_type: Prospective cohort study with propensity score matching
articles.population: Patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty in Finland between April 2021 and May 2023
articles.sample_size: 1,318 robotic-assisted procedures matched with 1,318 conventional procedures
articles.outcomes: Implant survival and revision rates within 12 months, with separate analysis for infection-related revisions
articles.take_home: Robotic-assisted and conventional knee replacement had similar overall revision rates at 12 months, but robotic-assisted surgery showed fewer revisions due to infection. The study found no clear advantage for robotic-assisted surgery in terms of overall implant survival.

articles.title: The Oxford Hip and Knee Scores in patients undergoing hip and knee arthroplasty: cross-cultural validation study based on 110,000 patients.
articles.authors: Ingelsrud LH, Sabah SA, Bohm E, Christensen KB, Troelsen A, Price AJ, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary hip or knee arthroplasty for osteoarthritis
articles.sample_size: 110,000 patients (21,108 English hip; 28,230 English knee; 36,792 Dutch hip; 29,651 Dutch knee; 815 Danish hip; 1,015 Danish knee; 590 French hip; 459 French knee)
articles.outcomes: Measurement invariance of Oxford Hip Score and Oxford Knee Score across English, Dutch, Danish, and French language versions using confirmatory factor analysis
articles.take_home: The Oxford Hip and Knee Scores work reliably across English, Dutch, Danish, and French versions, meaning doctors can fairly compare patient results between different countries. The scores measure the same thing regardless of language, so differences reflect real differences in patient outcomes rather than translation issues.

articles.title: Nordic hip fracture registries: comparisons toward a minimal common and standardized Nordic Hip Fracture Dataset (Nordic-HFD).
articles.authors: Schmidt CR, Palm H, Viberg B, Hedstrom M, Wolf O, Rogmark C, et al.
articles.population: Hip fracture patients in Denmark, Norway, and Sweden
articles.outcomes: Identification of 30 variables suitable for a standardized Nordic Hip Fracture Dataset, including demographic, surgical, postoperative, complications and patient-reported outcomes domains
articles.take_home: Researchers found it is feasible to create a standardized hip fracture dataset across Nordic countries using existing national registries, though some variables like mobility and complications need clearer definitions before use.

articles.title: The accuracy of radiographic peer review in identifying primary hip and knee arthroplasties at higher risk of early aseptic revision: an observational cohort study from the JointCare registry of South Africa.
articles.authors: Dymond ASD, Learmonth ID, Firer P, Diayar A
articles.population: Patients who underwent primary hip or knee arthroplasty surgery
articles.sample_size: 7,218 arthroplasties performed between January 2020 and June 2023
articles.outcomes: Aseptic revision rates compared against radiographic peer review scores (good, acceptable, or suboptimal)
articles.take_home: Surgeons' expert review of X-rays after hip and knee replacement surgery can identify operations at higher risk of needing revision surgery due to aseptic failure. Arthroplasties rated as suboptimal were 9 times more likely to require aseptic revision than those rated as good.

articles.title: Periarticular Hardware Retention does not Increase Reoperation Risk in Conversion Total Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Tantikosol P, Apinyakul R, Wong HJ, Amanatullah DF, Huddleston JI, Maloney WJ, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing conversion or primary total knee arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 320 patients (171 no hardware, 90 minor hardware, 59 major hardware)
articles.outcomes: Reoperation risk, operative time, blood loss, length of stay, complications, and patient-reported outcome measures (UCLA Activity Score and VR-12 Health Survey)
articles.take_home: Retaining metal hardware around the knee during knee replacement surgery does not increase the need for further operations, although surgery takes longer and involves more blood loss when major hardware is left in place. Patient satisfaction at two years was similar regardless of whether hardware was retained.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence-based versus conventional preoperative templating for tibial and femoral component size estimation in total knee arthroplasty: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Jancevski T, Mora L, Borse AM, Garcia Cortes DA, Martins EC
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 8 studies included
articles.outcomes: Accuracy of AI-assisted versus conventional preoperative templating in predicting exact femoral and tibial component size; short-term functional scores at 3 months
articles.take_home: CT-based AI planning may help predict the correct knee implant size better than standard X-ray templating, but the benefit is modest and not certain. Both methods performed similarly on functional outcomes 3 months after surgery.

articles.title: Changes in the Management of Periprosthetic Joint Infection Over the Past 50 Years.
articles.authors: Abedi AA, Pourbozorg G, Abdou M, Hoveidaei AH, Parvizi J, Citak M
articles.population: Patients with periprosthetic joint infection following joint arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Changes in prevention, diagnosis, and treatment approaches to periprosthetic joint infection over 50 years
articles.take_home: The management of joint infections around artificial joints has shifted from basic approaches to more scientific and tailored strategies, now using blood tests, fluid analysis, and genetic techniques to diagnose infections accurately and guide individualised treatment options.

articles.title: Orthopaedic surgeons' perceptions of individual feedback from a national arthroplasty quality register : a phenomenographic study.
articles.authors: Jolback P, Mohaddes M, Sundberg F
articles.population: Swedish orthopaedic surgeons and trainees
articles.sample_size: 19 participants (15 specialists and 4 trainees) from 15 hospitals
articles.outcomes: Four distinct perceptions of individual surgeon feedback from national arthroplasty register: professional development, risk of unfair criticism, potential harm to patient focus, and questioning of programme necessity
articles.take_home: Orthopaedic surgeons have mixed views about receiving individual performance feedback from national hip replacement registers. Whilst some see it as helpful for professional development, others worry it could lead to unfair criticism, shift focus away from what is best for patients, or duplicate existing local feedback systems.

articles.title: Predictors of Inability to Kneel and/or Squat One Year after Knee Arthroplasty in a Southeast Asian Population.
articles.authors: Sethi E, Mohan R, Leng TT, Kunnasegaran R, Jie Michael YG, Ho Poh W, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary knee arthroplasty in a Southeast Asian population
articles.sample_size: 888 knees in 830 patients
articles.outcomes: Ability to kneel and squat at one year after surgery, with predictive factors including range of motion, flexion, kneeling confidence, body mass index, age, and sex
articles.take_home: Only about 30-42% of patients could kneel and squat one year after knee replacement surgery. Better results were linked to greater flexibility after surgery, higher body mass index, higher age, and male sex, suggesting that improved preoperative fitness and realistic counselling might help more patients regain these important activities.

articles.title: The Risk Analysis Index is Superior to the Modified 5-Factor Frailty Index for Predicting 30-Day Mortality Following Arthroplasty for Femoral Neck Fractures.
articles.authors: Parisier E, Koltenyuk V, Gupta N, Wang L, Perugini A, Weick J
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using national database
articles.population: Patients aged 18 years or older undergoing hip replacement surgery for femoral neck fractures
articles.sample_size: 14,913 patients
articles.outcomes: 30-day mortality after hip replacement surgery, and comparison of two frailty assessment tools (Risk Analysis Index and Modified 5-Item Frailty Index) in predicting mortality
articles.take_home: The Risk Analysis Index was better at predicting which patients would die within 30 days of hip replacement surgery for femoral neck fractures compared to the Modified 5-Item Frailty Index. This suggests the Risk Analysis Index may be more useful for doctors to assess surgical risk before operating on frail patients with hip fractures.

articles.title: Dual Eligibility Status Is Associated With Lower Surgeon Reimbursement Despite Greater Patient Complexity in Primary Total Joint Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Persaud SG, Kucherina A, Ortiz S, Burgio C, Zepeda KE, Vigdorchik JM, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cross-sectional analysis of Medicare database
articles.population: Surgeons performing primary total hip and knee replacements in 2023
articles.sample_size: 4,506 hip surgeons performing 161,221 procedures; 6,618 knee surgeons performing 297,919 procedures
articles.outcomes: Mean standardised Medicare reimbursement per procedure, stratified by proportion of dual-eligible patients (Medicare and Medicaid)
articles.take_home: Surgeons treating more patients eligible for both Medicare and Medicaid received lower payment per operation, even though these patients had more complex health needs. This suggests the current payment system may inadvertently pay less to surgeons serving the most disadvantaged patients.

articles.title: Risk of venous thromboembolism after knee, hip, or shoulder arthroplasty : a retrospective cohort study of 476,620 procedures using linked hospital and primary care data.
articles.authors: Swain S, Leith N, Brown S, Wright Drakesmith C, Rees JL, Bankhead C, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing knee, hip, or shoulder arthroplasty in the UK
articles.sample_size: 476,620 procedures
articles.outcomes: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) within six months of surgery
articles.take_home: Overall VTE rates after joint replacement surgery were 1.5%, with rates declining over time for hip and knee surgery. The introduction of national guidelines did not significantly reduce VTE rates in knee and hip surgery, though shoulder surgery showed a 9% decrease after 2018 guidelines were introduced.

articles.title: Hip arthroplasty following proximal femoral tumour resection in children : the impact of age and articulation on implant survival and the outcomes following acetabular revision.
articles.authors: Baird CAE, Green N, Evans S, Kurisunkal V, Parry MC, Stevenson J
articles.population: Children aged 2 to 16 years who had hip replacement after removal of a malignant bone tumour in the upper thighbone
articles.sample_size: 60 patients (41 hemiarthroplasty, 19 total hip arthroplasty)
articles.outcomes: Implant survival rates, revision-free survival, modes of implant failure, outcomes after revision surgery
articles.take_home: Very young children (12 years and under) have a high risk of needing further surgery within ten years after hip replacement, regardless of replacement type. Older teenagers (over 12 years) who receive a full hip replacement do better than those who receive a partial replacement, though full replacement carries a small risk of early dislocation after surgery.

articles.title: A prospective double-blinded randomized controlled trial comparing conventional jig-based versus robotic arm-assisted medial unicompartmental knee arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Kayani B, Fontalis A, Tahmassebi J, Konan S, Plastow R, Wazir U, et al.
articles.population: Patients with symptomatic medial compartment knee osteoarthritis
articles.sample_size: 107 patients (52 conventional jig-based, 55 robotic arm-assisted)
articles.outcomes: Component positioning accuracy, inpatient pain scores, opioid consumption, length of hospital stay, Oxford Knee Score, Knee Injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score, Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Arthritis Index, Forgotten Joint Score
articles.take_home: Robotic arm-assisted knee replacement achieved more accurate component positioning, caused less pain in hospital, required fewer strong painkillers, and allowed faster discharge compared to conventional surgery. At two years, both approaches improved knee function similarly, though patients who had robotic surgery reported better overall joint feeling in their knee at six months and two years.

articles.title: Locking plate fixation compared with tension-band wiring for patellar fractures: a multicentre randomized controlled trial.
articles.authors: Larsen P, Thorninger R, Severinsen RP, Beuke JC, Jensen SS, Rasmussen MK, et al.
articles.study_type: Patient and assessor-blinded multicentre randomized controlled trial
articles.population: Adults with displaced patellar fracture requiring surgery
articles.sample_size: 122 participants (63 locking plate fixation, 59 tension-band wiring)
articles.outcomes: Patient-reported knee function using KOOS at 12 months; secondary outcomes included hardware removal, fixation failure, and reoperation rates
articles.take_home: Locking plate fixation produced better patient-reported knee function than tension-band wiring at 12 months, particularly for symptoms, sport and recreation activities, and quality of life. Tension-band wiring had higher rates of hardware removal, fixation failure, and need for further surgery.

articles.title: Total ankle arthroplasty via lateral transfibular approach with and without concomitant subtalar arthrodesis : radiological alignment, patient-reported outcomes, and range of motion at >/= five-year follow-up.
articles.authors: Constantinescu SA, Barbero A, Carfi C, Crippa Orlandi N, Bonzano C, Indino C, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing total ankle arthroplasty via lateral transfibular approach, with and without concomitant subtalar joint arthrodesis
articles.sample_size: 119 patients (50 with subtalar arthrodesis, 69 without)
articles.outcomes: Foot and Ankle Outcome Score, pain scores, quality of life questionnaire scores, ankle range of motion, radiological alignment, and complications at 5+ year follow-up
articles.take_home: Both groups showed significant improvement in pain and function at five years, with no meaningful differences between having ankle replacement alone or combined with subtalar fusion. The combined approach appears safe and effective for selected patients with arthritis in both joints.

articles.title: Five-year survival and complications of more than 300 articulating high-dose antibiotic spacers in two-stage revision total hip arthroplasties for infection.
articles.authors: Weintraub MT, Midthun WR, Pagnano MW, Taunton MJ, Sierra RJ, Mabry TM, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing two-stage hip replacement surgery for chronic hip joint infection
articles.sample_size: 298 patients (302 hip replacements)
articles.outcomes: Five-year infection-free survival, rerevision rates, dislocation, fracture, and hip function scores
articles.take_home: This type of antibiotic spacer used during two-stage hip replacement for infection had an 89% success rate at five years with no recurrent infection. Spacer dislocation was the main complication occurring in about 5% of patients, and if it happened, it increased the risk of dislocation after the final replacement was fitted.

articles.title: Impact of combined medial and lateral bone marrow lesions on clinical outcomes after medial unicompartmental knee arthroplasty : a retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Cao G, Wang A, Liu Q, Liu J, Liu Y, Huang Y
articles.population: Patients undergoing medial unicompartmental knee arthroplasty with preoperative MRI
articles.sample_size: 124 patients (86 with medial bone marrow lesions only, 38 with medial and lateral bone marrow lesions)
articles.outcomes: Pain (Numeric Rating Scale), function (Oxford Knee Score), radiological progression, mechanical alignment, and minimal clinically important difference achievement
articles.take_home: Patients undergoing partial knee replacement for arthritis who have bone marrow lesions in both the damaged and undamaged compartments had similar pain relief, functional improvement and long-term results compared to those with lesions in only the damaged compartment.

articles.title: Does transposition osteotomy of the acetabulum alter the natural history of developmental dysplasia of the hip?
articles.authors: Tanaka S, Fujii M, Kawano S, Ueno M, Oba Y, Morimoto T
articles.population: Patients with developmental dysplasia of the hip, borderline developmental dysplasia of the hip, or normal hips
articles.sample_size: 683 hips treated with transposition osteotomy and 353 contralateral native hips
articles.outcomes: 20-year cumulative probability of failure (progression to Tonnis grade 3 or conversion to total hip arthroplasty) and progression of osteoarthritis
articles.take_home: In severe hip dysplasia, acetabular transposition surgery improved long-term hip survival to 88% at 20 years compared with 69% without surgery. In borderline dysplasia, surgery did not significantly prevent joint failure but did slow osteoarthritis progression.

articles.title: Secondary patella resurfacing following primary total knee arthroplasty : patient-reported outcomes, satisfaction, and patient-acceptable symptom state.
articles.authors: Clement ND, Parsons T, Botfield-Gray T, Plastow R, Afzal I, Kader N, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing secondary patella resurfacing after primary total knee replacement
articles.sample_size: 182 patients (158 at one year follow-up, 143 at two years)
articles.outcomes: Oxford Knee Score, quality of life (EQ-5D and EQ-VAS), patient satisfaction, and patient-acceptable symptom state thresholds
articles.take_home: Secondary patella resurfacing led to meaningful improvements in knee function and quality of life, with about 80-86% of patients satisfied at follow-up. Patients were more likely to be satisfied if they were happy with their original knee replacement and if surgery was done more than 2.5 years after the first operation.

articles.title: Patient, surgeon, and institutional variation in dual-mobility component use in primary total hip arthroplasty : a retrospective cohort study using data from the National Joint Registry Study.
articles.authors: Zucker BE, Howard JT, Whitehouse MR, Judge A
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty in England
articles.sample_size: 238,455 primary hip replacements, of which 7,032 received dual-mobility components
articles.outcomes: Variation in dual-mobility component use attributable to patient, surgeon, and institutional factors
articles.take_home: Surgeon and hospital practice patterns were the main drivers of dual-mobility component use, accounting for over half of all variation, rather than patient characteristics alone. This suggests some variation may not reflect appropriate patient selection and better guidance is needed to standardise when these components should be used.

articles.title: Effects of Capacity-Related Delay to Hip Fracture Surgery on Mortality: A Matched-Cohort Study.
articles.authors: King SW, Wakefield SM, Giannoudis VP, Relton SD, Giannoudis PV, Pandit HG, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study with propensity-score matching
articles.population: Patients aged 65 years and over with hip fracture treated operatively at a UK teaching hospital
articles.sample_size: 2,358 eligible patients (1,087 timely surgery, 1,271 capacity-delayed surgery)
articles.outcomes: Mortality at 30 days and 365 days after hip fracture surgery
articles.take_home: Delays to hip fracture surgery caused by lack of operating theatre capacity were linked to a higher risk of death within one year, with the greatest risk in the first month. Frailer patients were most affected by these delays.

articles.title: An Acta Orthopaedica educational article: Current strategies for meniscal preservation in anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction.
articles.authors: Visnes H, Inderhaug E
articles.population: Patients undergoing anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction with concomitant meniscal injuries
articles.outcomes: Meniscal repair techniques and outcomes, osteoarthritis risk, repair survival rates
articles.take_home: Repairing meniscal tears alongside anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction is now preferred over removal whenever possible, as evidence shows this preserves knee health and reduces the risk of arthritis. Different tear types have proven repair techniques, such as transtibial repair for posterior root tears and all-inside methods for bucket-handle tears.

articles.title: Similar 2 year migration patterns for a shortened and a distally reduced stem design in uncemented total hip arthroplasty: a randomized controlled trial using radiostereometric analysis.
articles.authors: Koster L, Kaptein BL, Goorden E, Bell CAMP, Nelissen RGHH
articles.study_type: Randomized controlled trial using radiostereometric analysis
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary minimally invasive anterior-supine surgical total hip arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 50 patients (15 Microplasty stems, 20 Reduced Distal stems)
articles.outcomes: Subsidence and retroversion at 2 years; stem migration patterns; patient-reported outcome measures; clinical and radiological scores; adverse events
articles.take_home: Both the shortened hip stem and the standard-length stem with reduced distal width showed similar patterns of movement in the first 2 years after surgery, with both designs remaining stable from 6 weeks onwards. Although some initial movement occurred, it was not considered clinically important and there were no significant differences between the two stem designs.

articles.title: Patients' choice of healthcare provider for primary hip and knee arthroplasty: a national register-based observational cohort study of 62,676 patients from Norway, 2014-2018.
articles.authors: Hauglann B, Kjaervik C, Stensland E, Tesfay Y, Fenstad AM, Furnes O, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary hip and knee replacement surgery in Norway
articles.outcomes: Willingness to travel (in minutes) for different provider attributes including dedicated surgical units, regional location, surgical volume, proximity of family, and waiting times
articles.take_home: Patients were willing to travel substantially further for providers with dedicated elective surgical units (average 156 minutes extra) and those in their own health authority region (70 minutes extra). However, older patients, those with more health conditions, and those with lower education or income were less willing to travel, suggesting that choice of hospital is not equally available to all patients.

articles.title: Similar 1-year tibial implant migration, but higher continuous migration with cementless fixation: a retrospective RSA study of 990 patients with moderate to severe knee osteoarthritis.
articles.authors: Dal JM, Linde KN, Rytter S, Koppens D, Karim MAS, Stilling M
articles.study_type: Retrospective analysis of prospective clinical cohort using radiostereometric analysis
articles.population: Patients with moderate to severe knee osteoarthritis undergoing total or unicompartmental knee arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 990 patients (610 severe osteoarthritis, 380 moderate osteoarthritis)
articles.outcomes: Tibial implant migration measured by radiostereometric analysis at 1, 2, and 5 years; continuous migration between years 1 and 2; comparison between cemented and cementless fixation
articles.take_home: At one year, implant movement was similar regardless of osteoarthritis severity. However, patients with severe osteoarthritis who received cementless implants had a 73% higher risk of ongoing implant movement between years 1 and 2, which could increase the risk of needing revision surgery.
